dedupe_keys.name: laharz t semi automated regional hazard mapping of tailings storage facility failure flows ubc recalibrated laharz

description: LAHARZ-T is an empirical model for mapping areas that could be inundated by tailings flows after a tailings storage facility (TSF) failure, developed at the University of British Columbia by recalibrating LAHARZ, a GIS program originally built for mapping lahar inundation from volcanoes. The article read on 2026-09-28 (Resources, 24 September 2022) explains that LAHARZ-T uses empirical equations to predict the inundated planimetric and cross-sectional areas of a valley as a function of tailings flow volume, gives a first-order screening of downstream areas at risk, and demonstrates a regional application to 46 TSFs across Canada, while noting that variability in tailings properties and site conditions cannot be fully represented. Coverage is the Canadian demonstration, with a method usable elsewhere. Access is free through the open-access paper; no software licence is stated, and whether the recalibrated code is released is not stated on the page read. Caveats: results are regional screening, not dam-breach hydraulics. It supports hazard exposure screening of roads, rail, pipelines and settlements below mine tailings dams. Related records: case_study-feijao-dam-i-failure-expert-panel and case_study-mount-polley-tailings-breach-review document the failures such models address.
